A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and applied a novel statistical model to estimate intrafamiliar correlations of clinical traits in a rare autosomal dominant disease.
intrafamilial phenotypic correlations can be estimated using survival techniques in continuous variables with censoring and using negative-binomial gamma mixtures in discrete variables.
intrafamilial genetic factors play an important role in determining the clinical variability of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intrafamilial genetic correlations can be measured in a wide variety of clinical traits, including continuous, discrete, and survival traits.

survival and negative-binomial gamma models are useful for estimating intrafamilial (and perhaps other) correlations in clinical traits with right-censored and/or discrete distributions, respectively.
the intrafamilial phenotypic correlations in a disease can vary by type of mutation and by clinical manifestation.
